correctness.rationale: The Stewart--Sierpiński criterion specializes an exact-two-prime practical integer to \(2^a p^b\) with odd prime \(p\le 2^{a+1}\). Splitting the \(b=1\) count at \(m=\lfloor(\log_2 X-1)/2\rfloor\) gives two dyadic prime sums. Uniform prime-number-theorem estimates on \(1\le s<4\) yield leading terms \(4\,2^m/(m\log 2)\) and \(2s\,2^m/(m\log 2)\). For \(b\ge2\), the admissible-prime bound \(p\le\min\{2^{a+1},(X2^{-a})^{1/2}\}\) gives \(O(X^{1/3}\log X)=o(\sqrt X/\log X)\). With \(\sqrt X=2^m\sqrt{2s}\) and \(\log X=2m\log2\,(1+o(1))\), this reconstructs \((8+4s)/\sqrt{2s}\), whose minimum is \(8\) at \(s=2\) and endpoint value is \(6\sqrt2\). The finite verifier was inspected only as corroboration, not as proof of the asymptotic.
